name: ScyllaDB
model: Cassandra-compatible tables queried with CQL (plus a DynamoDB-compatible API, Alternator); rows grouped by partition key
engine_note: C++ rewrite of Cassandra's design: LSM tree (commit log, memtable, SSTables) on a shard-per-CPU-core engine (Seastar)
consistency: As Cassandra: tunable per query (ONE, QUORUM, ALL), so reads at low levels can be stale; single-partition writes atomic; lightweight transactions (Paxos) for compare-and-set. Commit log fsync every 10 s by default. Schema and topology changes use Raft.

jepsen.finding: Lightweight transactions showed split-brain and stale reads even in healthy clusters, and normal writes lacked the documented isolation; LWT bugs fixed by 4.2.1 and 4.3, the isolation claim was corrected in docs.

scaling: Add nodes or bigger machines (one shard per core); data spread by partition key, and tablets (on by default for new keyspaces) move small ranges between nodes automatically.
licence: ScyllaDB Software License Agreement v1.1 (source-available; free use capped at 10 TB storage and 50 vCPUs)

licence_events.event: ScyllaDB announces it will drop the AGPL open source edition (6.2 is the last) and ship one source-available product from 2025.1
ScyllaDB 2025.1.0, the first unified release under the source-available licence, tagged
Licence updated to v1.1: free use limited to 'Never Customers' (no paid relationship in the last 12 months) within 10 TB and 50 vCPUs

version_note: Date is the scylla-2026.3.2 tag commit; no GitHub release object exists. A 2026.3.3 candidate was tagged 2026-10-04.
reach: Reach for it when you need Cassandra-style scale with fewer, bigger machines and lower tail latency, and the licence limits or a paid licence suit you.
avoid: Avoid when you need joins or multi-partition transactions, want an OSI open source licence, or exceed 10 TB / 50 vCPUs without paying.
escape: Writes outgrow one machine and you want Cassandra's model with lower latency per node.
chat: Message history partitioned by chat id at very large scale (Discord moved from Cassandra to it); overkill for most apps.
notes: Licence v1.1 (last updated 2026-04-12) is stricter than the original 2024 terms: existing commercial customers get no free licence at all (except non-production CI/testing within the limit), and modified versions are assigned to ScyllaDB. Dates for 2025.1.0 and 2026.3.2 are tag commit dates, not announcement dates. scylla.yaml at tag 2026.3.2 ships tablets_mode_for_new_keyspaces: enabled. Discord migration: Discord engineering blog 'How Discord Stores Trillions of Messages' (2023, not re-read here). The Jepsen report tested 4.2-rc3 (AGPL era).
